questions.questionText: Your company wants to migrate an application to Google Cloud exactly as it runs currently on-premises, without making any changes to the application code or the operating system. Which workload disposition strategy is this?

explanation.general explanation: Rehost (also known as 'Lift and Shift') involves moving a workload from on-premises to the cloud without modifying the application code or the underlying operating system environment.

why other options are wrong.Replatform: Replatforming involves making minor optimizations (like moving to a managed database) without changing the core application code.
why other options are wrong.Refactor: Refactoring involves rewriting or significantly altering the application code to make it cloud-native.
why other options are wrong.Repurchase: Repurchasing involves dropping the existing application and moving to a SaaS alternative.

questions.questionText: During a migration assessment, you decide to move a self-managed, on-premises MySQL database to Cloud SQL. The application code connecting to the database requires only a minor configuration change to point to the new IP address. Which workload disposition strategy does this represent?

explanation.general explanation: Replatform (also known as 'Lift and Optimize') involves moving a workload to the cloud and taking advantage of managed services (like Cloud SQL instead of self-managed MySQL) without changing the core architecture or application code.

why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehosting would mean spinning up a Compute Engine VM and manually installing and managing MySQL, exactly like on-premises.
why other options are wrong.Refactor: Refactoring involves significant code changes, such as rewriting the app to use Cloud Spanner or a NoSQL database.
why other options are wrong.Retain: Retain means keeping the database on-premises.

questions.questionText: Your organization decides to completely rewrite a monolithic legacy application into decoupled microservices using Cloud Run and Pub/Sub. Which workload disposition strategy is this?

explanation.general explanation: Refactor (or Rearchitect) involves rewriting the application code and fundamentally changing its architecture to become fully cloud-native, utilizing services like serverless compute and managed messaging.

why other options are wrong.Repurchase: Repurchase involves buying a completely new commercial software product (SaaS).
why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehost involves no code changes, just moving the monolith to a VM.
why other options are wrong.Replatform: Replatform involves minor optimizations, not a complete rewrite into microservices.

questions.questionText: Your company currently maintains a highly customized, on-premises email and collaboration server. To save on maintenance costs, management decides to abandon this custom system and migrate all users to Google Workspace. Which workload disposition strategy was applied?

explanation.general explanation: Repurchase (also known as 'Drop and Shop') involves moving away from an existing on-premises application by purchasing a completely different cloud-based SaaS product, such as Google Workspace or Salesforce.

why other options are wrong.Refactor: Refactoring would mean rewriting the code of the custom email server.
why other options are wrong.Replatform: Replatforming would mean running the custom email server on GCP managed services.
why other options are wrong.Retire: While the old system is retired, the workload (email) is being actively replaced by a SaaS purchase, which explicitly categorizes it as Repurchase.

questions.questionText: During the discovery phase of your cloud migration, you find an application server that has not received any user traffic in over two years. The business confirms the application is no longer needed. What is the most appropriate disposition strategy?

explanation.general explanation: Retire means decommissioning or shutting down an application that is no longer useful to the business. This is a critical step in migration planning to avoid moving and paying for unnecessary workloads in the cloud.

why other options are wrong.Retain: Retain means keeping the workload running on-premises, which costs money and resources for a dead application.
why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehosting an unused application to the cloud incurs unnecessary compute costs.
why other options are wrong.Repurchase: There is no need to purchase a replacement for an application that is no longer needed.

questions.questionText: An enterprise has a highly sensitive workload that runs on a specialized legacy mainframe. Current compliance regulations mandate that this specific system must remain physically inside the company's own data center. Which disposition strategy should you apply to this workload?

explanation.general explanation: Retain (or 'Leave as is') is the strategy of keeping a workload in its current on-premises environment. This is typically chosen when workloads are running on unsupported legacy hardware (like mainframes) or are bound by strict regulatory constraints that prevent cloud migration.

why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehosting moves the workload to the cloud, violating the physical location requirement.
why other options are wrong.Replatform: Replatforming moves the workload to the cloud.
why other options are wrong.Refactor: Refactoring rewrites the workload for the cloud.

questions.questionText: Your company has hundreds of virtual machines running on VMware vSphere in an on-premises data center. The data center lease expires in one month, requiring the fastest possible migration to Google Cloud with zero changes to the VMs. Which GCP service directly supports this 'Rehost' strategy?

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud VMware Engine (GCVE) provides a fully managed VMware vSphere environment natively in Google Cloud. It allows organizations to lift-and-shift (Rehost) their existing VMware workloads rapidly without changing tooling, networking, or VM configurations.

why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): GKE requires containerizing the workloads, which is a Replatform or Refactor strategy, not a zero-change Rehost.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Standard: App Engine is a PaaS that requires application code, not whole VMware VMs.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: Cloud Run runs stateless containers, not VMware virtual machines.

questions.questionText: Which migration disposition strategy generally offers the fastest time-to-cloud and the lowest initial migration risk, but yields the lowest long-term cloud-native benefits (like auto-scaling)?

explanation.general explanation: Rehost (Lift and Shift) is the fastest and least risky migration strategy because you are simply copying VMs as-is. However, because the application isn't optimized for the cloud, it misses out on native features like granular auto-scaling, serverless pricing, and managed backups.

why other options are wrong.Refactor: Refactor takes the longest time and highest initial risk due to rewriting code, though it yields the highest long-term benefits.
why other options are wrong.Repurchase: Repurchase requires migrating data and retraining users on a new SaaS system, which can be time-consuming.
why other options are wrong.Replatform: Replatforming is faster than refactoring, but slightly slower and riskier than a pure Rehost due to minor optimizations.

questions.questionText: Your team decides to move a workload to the cloud. The source code for the application was lost years ago, and the original developers have left the company. The application is critical and must remain unchanged. Which migration strategy is your only viable option?

explanation.general explanation: Because you do not have the source code, you cannot rewrite or easily modify the application. Rehosting (lifting and shifting the entire VM as a black box) is the only way to move the workload to the cloud without needing access to the source code.

why other options are wrong.Refactor: Refactoring requires rewriting the source code, which is impossible without it.
why other options are wrong.Replatform: Replatforming often requires minor configuration or dependency changes in the codebase.
why other options are wrong.Repurchase: Repurchasing replaces the app entirely, which violates the requirement that the application 'must remain unchanged'.

questions.questionText: Which Google Cloud tool is specifically designed to support the 'Rehost' strategy by orchestrating the automated replication and conversion of on-premises VMs directly into Compute Engine instances?
options: Google Cloud Migrate to Virtual Machines
correctAnswers: Google Cloud Migrate to Virtual Machines

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud Migrate to Virtual Machines (formerly Migrate for Compute Engine) is the dedicated tool for orchestrating 'Lift and Shift' (Rehost) migrations. It streams VM disks into Google Cloud and converts them into native Compute Engine instances.

why other options are wrong.Google Cloud Storage Transfer Service: This service moves objects/files from on-prem or other clouds to Cloud Storage, not live VMs.
why other options are wrong.Database Migration Service: DMS is for replatforming databases to Cloud SQL or AlloyDB, not for moving full VMs.
why other options are wrong.Dataflow: Dataflow is for data processing and ETL pipelines, not VM migration.

questions.questionText: You are assessing an application that writes terabytes of log files to local disk storage on-premises. As part of the migration, you decide the application will instead write these files directly to a Cloud Storage bucket using the Google Cloud Client Libraries, but the rest of the application remains on VMs. This minor optimization is an example of which strategy?

explanation.general explanation: Replatforming (Lift and Optimize) involves making small, targeted changes to an application so it can take advantage of cloud-native managed services (like swapping local disk writes for Cloud Storage API calls) without completely rewriting the core application architecture.

why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehosting would mean attaching a persistent disk to the VM in GCP to act exactly like the local disk on-premises, without changing the application code to use Cloud Storage.
why other options are wrong.Repurchase: Repurchasing means dropping the app for a SaaS.
why other options are wrong.Retire: Retire means shutting the app down.

questions.questionText: A primary business driver for migrating to Google Cloud is to scale an application's compute footprint to exactly zero when there is no traffic to save costs. Which workload disposition strategy MUST you use to achieve this if the application is currently a legacy VM-based monolith?

explanation.general explanation: To scale an application down to zero, it must be deployed on serverless platforms like Cloud Run or App Engine Standard. A legacy VM-based monolith cannot run on these platforms without being completely rewritten (containerized, made stateless, etc.). This complete architectural change is Refactoring.

why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehosting moves the monolith to a Compute Engine VM. VMs do not natively scale to zero cost automatically based on incoming HTTP traffic.
why other options are wrong.Retain: Retaining keeps the workload on-premises, ignoring the business driver entirely.
why other options are wrong.Replatform: Replatforming might containerize the app for GKE, but standard GKE nodes do not scale to absolute zero cost as easily and natively as fully refactored serverless apps.

questions.questionText: Which two disposition strategies involve moving or replacing an application in the cloud with the LEAST amount of custom code rewriting required by your development team?

explanation.general explanation: Rehost (Lift and Shift) involves copying the VM exactly as-is without code changes. Repurchase involves moving to a vendor-provided SaaS product, which requires no custom coding from your team (only configuration and data migration). Both avoid source code rewrites.

why other options are wrong.Refactor: Refactor inherently means rewriting the application code to be cloud-native.
why other options are wrong.Rearchitect: Rearchitect is synonymous with Refactor; it involves significant code and architecture changes.

questions.questionText: Your company currently runs a self-managed Hadoop cluster on-premises. As part of your migration, you decide to move these Spark and Hadoop jobs to Cloud Dataproc. The jobs will run exactly as they did before, but you no longer manage the underlying infrastructure. Which disposition strategy is this?

explanation.general explanation: Moving from a self-managed open-source cluster to a managed cloud service equivalent (like Cloud Dataproc for Hadoop/Spark) without rewriting the actual data processing jobs is a classic example of Replatforming (Lift and Optimize).

why other options are wrong.Refactor: Refactoring would involve rewriting the Spark jobs into Apache Beam to run on Cloud Dataflow.
why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehosting would mean creating raw Compute Engine VMs and installing Hadoop manually, managing it exactly like on-premises.
why other options are wrong.Repurchase: Repurchasing would mean abandoning Hadoop entirely for a commercial SaaS data tool.

questions.questionText: During the discovery phase of a migration, you need a tool to automatically scan your on-premises data center, identify all virtual machines, assess their resource utilization, and recommend the best Google Cloud machine types. Which tool should you use?

explanation.general explanation: StratoZone is an assessment tool provided by Google Cloud. It automates the discovery of your on-premises IT infrastructure, providing cost estimates, resource mapping, and recommendations to help plan workload disposition strategies.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Build: Cloud Build is a CI/CD platform, not an infrastructure discovery tool.
why other options are wrong.Database Migration Service: DMS is for moving databases, not for general data center discovery and VM assessment.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Profiler: Cloud Profiler analyzes the performance of application code in production, not on-premises infrastructure assessment.

questions.questionText: You are migrating a fleet of 50 Windows Server 2008 VMs that run a legacy internal application. Upgrading the OS or application is not possible. Which workload disposition strategy is the most appropriate?

explanation.general explanation: When an application relies on a legacy OS that cannot be upgraded or modified, Rehost (Lift and Shift) is typically the only viable option to move it to the cloud. You copy the VM exactly as it is into Compute Engine.

why other options are wrong.Refactor: Refactoring requires modifying the application, which is stated as not possible.
why other options are wrong.Replatform: Replatforming would require the application to run on a modernized managed service or container, which a legacy Windows 2008 app typically cannot do without changes.
why other options are wrong.Repurchase: If an off-the-shelf alternative existed, repurchase would be an option, but for a legacy custom internal app with hard constraints, rehost is the standard approach.

questions.questionText: A workload assigned the 'Retain' disposition strategy will stay in your on-premises data center. However, you want to manage this on-premises workload using the exact same Kubernetes control plane you use for your Google Cloud workloads. Which Google Cloud technology supports this hybrid design?

explanation.general explanation: GKE Enterprise (formerly Anthos) allows you to run and manage Kubernetes clusters both in Google Cloud and on-premises using a single, unified control plane. It is the perfect solution for modernizing 'Retained' workloads in a hybrid environment.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: Cloud Run is a fully managed serverless platform that runs in Google Cloud, not on-premises.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine Sole-tenant nodes: Sole-tenant nodes are dedicated physical servers inside Google's data centers, not your on-premises data center.
why other options are wrong.Google Cloud VMware Engine: GCVE runs VMware workloads natively inside Google Cloud, not on-premises.

questions.questionText: Which two scenarios strongly indicate that a workload should be assigned a 'Retire' disposition strategy?
options: The application has been superseded by a newly developed internal system.
Network traffic logs show zero active users for the past 12 months.
The application requires ultra-low latency to a local factory floor machine.
The application's source code was lost by the original developers.
correctAnswers: The application has been superseded by a newly developed internal system.
Network traffic logs show zero active users for the past 12 months.

explanation.general explanation: A 'Retire' strategy means decommissioning the workload. This is appropriate when the application is redundant (superseded by a new system) or verifiably unused (zero active users).

why other options are wrong.The application requires ultra-low laten: This is a reason to 'Retain' the application on-premises, not retire it.
why other options are wrong.The application's source code was lost b: This is a constraint that forces a 'Rehost' strategy, but doesn't necessarily mean the application isn't critical and shouldn't be retired.

questions.questionText: Your team packages an existing web application into a Docker container without changing the application logic. You then deploy this container to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). Which migration strategy does this represent?

explanation.general explanation: Containerizing an existing application without rewriting its core logic is a classic Replatform (Lift and Optimize) strategy. You optimize the operational model (moving from VMs to orchestrated containers) while avoiding the deep code changes required for a true Refactor.

why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehost involves moving the entire VM as-is without containerizing it.
why other options are wrong.Repurchase: Repurchase is replacing the app with a SaaS.
why other options are wrong.Retire: Retire is shutting down the app.

questions.questionText: Which migration strategy requires the highest initial investment in developer time and testing, but typically results in the lowest long-term operational costs and highest scalability?

explanation.general explanation: Refactor (Rearchitect) involves rewriting the application to use cloud-native features like serverless, auto-scaling, and managed services. This requires significant upfront developer effort, but results in highly scalable, cost-efficient applications.

why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehost requires minimal developer time but retains the high operational overhead of managing raw VMs.
why other options are wrong.Replatform: Replatform requires less effort than Refactor and provides some optimizations, but less long-term efficiency than a fully refactored cloud-native app.
why other options are wrong.Retain: Retain requires zero migration effort but yields zero cloud benefits.

questions.questionText: You are using Database Migration Service (DMS) to move data from an on-premises PostgreSQL database to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL. The database schema and queries will remain identical. What workload disposition strategy is this?

explanation.general explanation: Moving from a self-managed database to a fully managed equivalent (like Cloud SQL) without changing the database schema or application queries is a Replatform strategy. You gain operational efficiencies without rewriting code.

why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehosting would mean running PostgreSQL on a Compute Engine VM.
why other options are wrong.Refactor: Refactoring would involve changing the database engine entirely (e.g., PostgreSQL to Cloud Spanner) and rewriting queries.
why other options are wrong.Repurchase: Repurchase is replacing the workload with a commercial SaaS.

questions.questionText: A critical on-premises application uses a self-managed Apache Kafka cluster for message queuing. To reduce operational burden, the architecture team decides to rewrite the application's messaging logic to use Google Cloud Pub/Sub instead. Which workload disposition strategy is this?

explanation.general explanation: Because the application's messaging logic must be actively rewritten to use a completely different, cloud-native messaging API (Pub/Sub instead of Kafka), this is a Refactor strategy.

why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehosting would mean moving the Kafka VMs as-is to Compute Engine.
why other options are wrong.Repurchase: The application isn't being abandoned for a SaaS product; its internal code is being modified.
why other options are wrong.Retire: The application is being modernized, not decommissioned.

questions.questionText: Your company has three separate HR applications that were accumulated through acquisitions. They all perform the same basic function. To reduce licensing and cloud migration costs, management decides to migrate only the best application to GCP and shut down the other two. What is the disposition strategy for the two shut-down applications?

explanation.general explanation: When applications are consolidated and redundant systems are deliberately shut down and not migrated, the disposition strategy applied to those redundant systems is 'Retire'.

why other options are wrong.Repurchase: No new software is being purchased; an existing internal app is being selected.
why other options are wrong.Retain: Retaining means keeping them running on-premises, but management explicitly decided to shut them down.
why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehosting would mean migrating them, which was explicitly avoided to save costs.

questions.questionText: A major enterprise is moving an on-premises Oracle database to Google Cloud. Because Oracle is highly proprietary and strict regarding licensing, the business decides to migrate the schema and application logic to a new PostgreSQL database running on AlloyDB. What disposition strategy does this represent?

explanation.general explanation: Moving from one database engine (Oracle) to a completely different one (PostgreSQL on AlloyDB) requires rewriting schemas, stored procedures, and application queries. This significant structural change classifies as a Refactor (or Rearchitect) strategy.

why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehosting would mean running Oracle on a Compute Engine VM.
why other options are wrong.Retain: Retaining would mean leaving Oracle on-premises.
why other options are wrong.Repurchase: Repurchasing means buying a SaaS application, not migrating database engines.

questions.questionText: Your development team decides to implement a 'Strangler Fig' pattern to slowly migrate an on-premises monolithic application. They replace one feature at a time with a new microservice hosted on Cloud Run, while the remaining monolith stays on-premises. Which disposition strategy is being applied to the modernized features?

explanation.general explanation: The Strangler Fig pattern is a classic Refactoring technique. It involves systematically rewriting portions of a legacy application into cloud-native microservices (like Cloud Run) until the entire original application is modernized and replaced.

why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehosting moves the entire monolith as-is without breaking it apart.
why other options are wrong.Repurchase: Repurchase drops the entire application for a vendor SaaS.
why other options are wrong.Retire: While the old monolith code is eventually retired, the strategy driving the migration of the features to the cloud is Refactoring.

questions.questionText: Which two scenarios strongly indicate that a workload should be assigned a 'Retain' disposition strategy?
options: The workload requires hardware that is physically attached to an on-premises manufacturing machine.
Data sovereignty laws dictate that the data cannot leave the physical borders of a country where Google Cloud has no region.
The source code for the application has been lost.
The data center lease is expiring in two weeks.
correctAnswers: The workload requires hardware that is physically attached to an on-premises manufacturing machine.
Data sovereignty laws dictate that the data cannot leave the physical borders of a country where Google Cloud has no region.

explanation.general explanation: A 'Retain' strategy means keeping the workload on-premises. This is necessary when physical proximity to non-cloud hardware is required (manufacturing machines) or when strict legal data sovereignty regulations forbid moving data to available public cloud regions.

why other options are wrong.The source code for the application has: This indicates a 'Rehost' strategy (moving the VM as a black box), not necessarily 'Retain'.
why other options are wrong.The data center lease is expiring in two: This is a strong driver for a rapid 'Rehost' migration, not retaining the workloads in a closing data center.

questions.questionText: What is the primary benefit of choosing a 'Replatform' strategy over a 'Rehost' strategy?
options: It reduces operational overhead by utilizing managed services while avoiding massive code rewrites.
It offers the fastest possible migration time.
It completely eliminates the need for any virtual machines or containers.
It allows you to abandon your custom application for a vendor SaaS product.
correctAnswers: It reduces operational overhead by utilizing managed services while avoiding massive code rewrites.

explanation.general explanation: Replatforming strikes a balance. It provides cloud benefits (like automated backups and patching via managed services like Cloud SQL) without the massive time and risk investment required to fully rewrite (Refactor) the application code.

why other options are wrong.It offers the fastest possible migration: Rehost is typically faster than Replatforming because it requires zero changes.
why other options are wrong.It completely eliminates the need for an: Replatforming often still uses containers (GKE) or PaaS environments, which may still run on underlying infrastructure.

questions.questionText: Your organization uses an old, custom-built issue tracking system. It is buggy, hard to maintain, and the developers who built it have left. You decide to migrate the team to Jira Software (a commercial SaaS product) instead of moving the old system to Google Cloud. What disposition strategy is this?

explanation.general explanation: Repurchase involves dropping an existing legacy application and replacing it with a commercially available off-the-shelf software or Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution.

why other options are wrong.Retire: While the old system is technically retired, the act of replacing the *workload* with a purchased product is categorized specifically as Repurchase.
why other options are wrong.Refactor: Refactoring would mean rewriting the custom issue tracker.
why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehosting would mean moving the buggy custom issue tracker to Compute Engine.

questions.questionText: An application is being migrated using the 'Rehost' strategy via Google Cloud Migrate to Virtual Machines. Which factor is completely irrelevant to the success of this specific migration strategy?
options: The programming language the application is written in.
The operating system of the source VM.
The network bandwidth available between on-premises and Google Cloud.
The total size of the VM's attached disks.
correctAnswers: The programming language the application is written in.

explanation.general explanation: A Rehost (Lift and Shift) migration moves the entire operating system and application as a black box. Because the code is not being modified, recompiled, or changed in any way, the programming language it is written in is irrelevant to the migration mechanism.

This is highly relevant. Migrate to Virtual Machines must support the specific OS (e.g., specific Linux/Windows versions) to successfully boot it in Compute Engine.
why other options are wrong.The network bandwidth available between: Bandwidth is critical to determine how long the VM disk replication will take.
why other options are wrong.The total size of the VM's attached disk: Disk size dictates migration time and storage costs, making it highly relevant.

questions.questionText: Which migration disposition strategy is most closely associated with the phrase 'Drop and Shop'?

explanation.general explanation: In cloud migration terminology, 'Repurchase' is often colloquially referred to as 'Drop and Shop' because you drop your existing legacy application and shop for a modern commercial SaaS alternative.

why other options are wrong.Rehost: Rehost is known as 'Lift and Shift'.
why other options are wrong.Replatform: Replatform is known as 'Lift and Optimize' or 'Lift and Shape'.
